sections.heading: Glamsterdam Devnet and Sepolia Status
sections.summary: Sepolia is stable post-fork; several Glamsterdam devnet nodes (Nimbus, Erigon, some Besu combos) are offline and need attention.
sections.body:
- Glamsterdam devnet: Nimbus and Erigon nodes are offline, as well as some Lighthouse/Grandine + Besu combinations. Client teams asked to investigate.
- Sepolia has been very stable since the fork, with nearly 100% participation after a few initially missed slots. All node operators came up after the fork.
- A mainnet shadow fork based on jochemnet was launched in two versions:
  - Version 1 tested the Glamsterdam fork transition and snap syncing; found stability and head-selection issues in several clients.
  - Version 2 launched this week post-fork with state bloat (64 KB contracts) for benchmarking. Wallet funding is still in progress; benchmarking scenarios will be run by Stefan and Lewis.

sections.heading: Hoodi Release Deadline
sections.summary: Client releases for Hoodi are needed by Friday, October 16th; Lodestar has already published its release.
sections.body:
- Reminder that all client releases targeting Hoodi must be ready by Friday, October 16th.
- Alex Stokes is working on the accompanying blog post, intended for publication that day.
- [Lodestar v1.50.0](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/releases/tag/v1.50.0) has been published.
- Client teams asked to notify Alex Stokes when their releases are available.

sections.heading: Proposer Selection Oversight
sections.summary: A proposer-selection manipulation via self-slashing was reported; consensus is to defer any fix to Hegota, not Glamsterdam.
sections.body:
- A report on ETH R&D described an issue where a proposer assigned to slot 31 could self-slash to manipulate the compute shuffle index, potentially inserting their own validator into proposer slots in the following two epochs.
  - PR: [consensus-specs #5733](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5733)
- The attack requires a validator to slash itself, making it economically unattractive; the attacker would also need specific conditions around epoch boundaries.
- Toni noted the same manipulation is possible via RANDAO, calling it a non-problem from the attacker's perspective.
- This is a consensus-breaking change; implementing it for Glamsterdam would risk breaking Sepolia and require managing two implementations.
- Dustin stated Thursday (ACD-C) is a non-starter for deciding this, given Hoodi releases are due Friday.
- Decision: push this fix to Hegota at the earliest. No support was expressed for including it in Glamsterdam.
  - Pawan, Enrico, and Dustin all agreed to defer.

sections.heading: Minimum Hardware Requirements for Glamsterdam
sections.summary: EIP-7870 sequential read/write specs are unrealistically low; agreement to update the living EIP rather than create a new one per fork.
sections.body:
- Jochem raised that [EIP-7870](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7870) specifies 500 MB/s sequential read/write, which is far too low for Glamsterdam given increased contract code size (24→64 KB), gas limit (60→200M), and cold account access cost (2600→3000 gas).
  - Worst-case Glamsterdam block runs in ~8 seconds on the current spec hardware, which is too slow.
  - Proposed increase to at least 1000 MB/s, preferably 2000 MB/s.
- Barnabas emphasized random 4K IOPS matter more than sequential throughput for EVM workloads; the new EIP proposal uses the same IOPS values.
  - Reference hardware: Samsung 970 EVO (15,000 IOPS at QD1).
- Maria and Ben Adams noted the current spec values never existed for NVMe drives at the specified capacity; specs are strangely low relative to what real nodes run.
- Dustin pushed back on the broader narrative, noting other dimensions (RAM, CPU) in EIP-7870 are already very high; Nimbus users run on 16 GB ARM SBCs successfully.
- Łukasz clarified the distinction: average blocks run fine on lower hardware, but recommended specs must handle worst-case (DoS) blocks.
- On format: consensus favored keeping EIP-7870 as a single living document rather than creating per-fork EIPs, to avoid confusion when users search for Ethereum hardware specs.
  - Łukasz and Pooja suggested including forward-looking requirements (e.g., Hegota) in the same EIP with explicit history per fork.
- Justin Traglia noted EIP-7870 defines "recommended" not "minimum" requirements; the two are often conflated.
  - Dustin called this a motte-and-bailey, since "recommended" gets treated as "minimum" in practice.
- PR to update EIP-7870: [ethereum/EIPs#12491](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12491); Jochem moved it to Review status.
  - Toni encouraged moving it from draft to ready for review.

sections.heading: Heze-devnet-2 Planning and Quick Slots
sections.summary: Heze-devnet-2 will include FOCIL, EIP-8015, EIP-8365, and EIP-8198 (quick slots) at 12-second slot duration, targeting late October.
sections.body:
- Justin Traglia proposed heze-devnet-2 include FOCIL (EIP-7805), EIP-8015 (remove deposit/eth1data fields), EIP-8365 (disallow new 0x00 validators), and EIP-8198 (quick slots).
- Target launch: October 28th at the latest, or as soon as 3 CL clients have support.
  - Barnabas preferred October 21 with 12s slots or October 28 with 10s slots.
- Quick slots (EIP-8198) slot duration: agreement to keep 12 seconds for heze-devnet-2.
  - Dustin stated Nimbus will not have quick slots support in this timeframe; if 10s is required, Nimbus likely won't join.
  - Teku, Lodestar, and Lighthouse already have quick slots implementations (Lodestar on trunk branch, ethrex added support for focil-devnet-2).
  - Matthew Keil and others agreed to keep 12-second slots.
- EIP-8198 quick slots spec to be merged into Heze consensus specs; Barnabas noted tooling-side blockers that need resolution.
  - EIP-8198 requires some EL support: [execution-specs PR #3703](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/pull/3703)
- Discussion of sub-slot deadline adjustments for shorter slots deferred; Barnabé Monnot noted attestation deadline has fixed overhead and should not scale linearly with slot time.
  - Toni and Jihoon agreed observation deadlines are easy to change; no rush to decide before Glamsterdam mainnet data is available.
- Prysm targeting October 28 for heze-devnet-2 readiness: [tracking issue](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/issues/17673)
- Lighthouse can have it by October 28.
- No objections raised to the overall plan.

sections.heading: Heze/Bogota Devnet Naming and Renaming
sections.summary: Devnets will be renamed from FOCIL/frames prefixes to Heze/Bogota; broad support expressed via chat reactions.
sections.body:
- Proposal to rename existing devnets to align with fork names rather than headliner EIP names:
  - focil-devnet-0 → heze-devnet-0, focil-devnet-1 → heze-devnet-1, focil-devnet-2 → heze-devnet-2
  - frames-devnet-0 → bogota-devnet-0, frames-devnet-1 → bogota-devnet-1
- EthPandaOps confirmed the rename is feasible; indexing will be preserved (e.g., heze-devnet-2, not heze-devnet-0).
- Going forward, devnets will use the fork name (e.g., Bogota, Heze) from the CFI stage rather than single-EIP headliner names.
- Broad support from chat reactions across multiple client teams.
- Test releases will also be renamed accordingly (e.g., `tests-bogota-devnet`).

sections.heading: Bogota-devnet-1 Launch and EL Updates
sections.summary: Bogota-devnet-1 (frames, keyed nonces, recent roots, transaction assertions) targets Thursday launch; a keyed-nonce spec clarification needs a test release update.
sections.body:
- Bogota-devnet-1 (formerly frames-devnet-1) includes EIP-8141 (frames), EIP-8250 (keyed nonces), EIP-8272 (recent roots), and EIP-7906 (transaction assertions).
- Test release [tests-frames-devnet@v1.0.0](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/releases/tag/tests-frames-devnet%40v1.0.0) was published Friday; ethrex and Nethermind already passing.
- One consensus-breaking clarification merged since the release: keyed nonces are added to block access lists (BAL), and keyed nonce contract now uses Nick's method for pre-fork deployment instead of fork-transition insertion.
  - Toni clarified this also affects floor gas calculation when combined with frame transactions, changing calldata prices.
- A v1.1.0 test release incorporating this change targeted for end of day; devnet launch on Thursday if clients have images ready.
- Stefan offered to prioritize devnet launch alongside shadow fork work.
- ethrex contributed test PRs: [#3756](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/pull/3756) for EIP-related changes and [#3757](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/pull/3757).

sections.heading: Future Hegota Devnet EIP Planning
sections.summary: Early sentiment favors adding SETCODEFROM, data repricing (EIP-8279), nonce bump (EIP-8253), and deactivate SELFDESTRUCT to upcoming devnets; formal decision deferred to next call.
sections.body:
- Spencer asked whether devnet EIP planning could be done further ahead (e.g., devnet+2 lookahead) to help client teams work ahead and reduce burnout.
  - Dustin cautioned against assuming outcomes of earlier devnets; CFI is meant to validate that EIPs work.
  - Matthew Keil warned against putting the cart before the horse, especially for quick slots.
  - Justin Florentine highlighted the risk of interaction effects (e.g., FOCIL + frames) and the need to test headliners together before layering more EIPs.
  - Spencer acknowledged the points and suggested discussing the process further at a future gathering.
- Concrete EIP suggestions for near-term devnets:
  - SETCODEFROM: Nethermind and Geth already implemented and passing EEST tests ([execution-specs PR #3769](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/pull/3769)). Carlos (CPerezz) noted it's the primary path for post-quantum migration.
  - Data repricing, especially EIP-8279 (more involved of the two): Toni argued including complex EIPs early helps debug them, citing EIP-8037 as precedent.
  - [EIP-8253](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8253) (nonce bump): behavior only at fork transition, so needs testing across as many devnets as possible. Jochem to open PR for devnet template accounts. Related clarification PR: [ethereum/EIPs#12456](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12456).
  - Deactivate SELFDESTRUCT: Maria suggested adding it early to remove edge cases from testing. Jochem noted EIP-8360 (TCREATE) should accompany it to address economic pattern changes, though Justin Florentine argued TCREATE testing is orthogonal.
- Toni's consolidated suggestion for next devnet additions: SETCODEFROM, data repricing, nonce bump, deactivate SELFDESTRUCT.
  - Also mentioned: EIP-8151 (Marc supportive).
- Decision deferred: Mario proposed using the [pm issue tracker](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/2264#issuecomment-6069170769) for async discussion, with a formal conclusion at the next ACDT call.
- CFI'd CL EIPs reference: [forkcast.org listing](https://forkcast.org/eips/?upgrade=Hegota&stage=Considered&layer=CL)

sections.heading: CL Breakout: v1.7.0-beta.4 and Spec PRs
sections.summary: CL spec v1.7.0-beta.4 published; IL deadline raise and produceBlockV4WithBid endpoint deferred to CL breakout discussion.
sections.body:
